preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain ownership through transferOwner/confirmOwner flow)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the mint() function to create new tokens for your address, increasing your token balance arbitrarily. Optionally, use freezeTransfers() to lock other users' transfers while you liquidate your newly minted tokens, or unfreezeTransfers() to enable transfers if currently frozen.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The LineAxis contract inherits from Owned and ERC20. The vulnerability is that the owner can call the mint() function to create arbitrary amounts of tokens for any address. Since the attacker needs to be the owner, we must first gain ownership through the transferOwner/confirmOwner flow or directly become owner through storage manipulation.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become the contract owner by either (a) using the transferOwner/confirmOwner flow if we can impersonate the current owner, or (b) directly overwriting the owner storage slot. 2. Call mint() to create tokens for ourselves. 3. Optionally unfreeze transfers if frozen to enable token movement.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the current owner and call transferOwner() to set ourselves as new owner. 2. Call confirmOwner() to become the actual owner. 3. Call mint() to create a large amount of tokens for our address. 4. Verify our balance increased.
